description:
WORKFLOW: Step 2 of 4 - Continue infrastructure design conversation
Send a user message to the active InsideOut session and receive the assistant reply.
The response contains a clean message from Riley - display it to the user.

⚠️ CRITICAL: DO NOT answer Riley's questions yourself! Forward questions to the user and wait for their response. NEVER fabricate or assume the user's answer, even if you think you know what they would say.
Examples of questions Riley asks that YOU MUST forward to the user:
- 'Any questions or tweaks to these details?'
- 'Ready for the cost estimate?'
- 'Do you want to change the stack/config?'
- 'Ready to proceed to Terraform?'
When Riley asks ANY question, STOP and wait for the user's answer!

📋 WORKFLOW PHASES: The typical flow is conversation → tfgenerate → tfdeploy
When terraform_ready=true appears in THIS tool's response, THEN you can call tfgenerate.
⚠️ DO NOT call tfgenerate until this tool returns! Wait for the response first.

🎯 KEY SIGNALS IN RESPONSE:
- `[TERRAFORM_READY: true]` → NOW you can call tfgenerate
- `[[BUTTON_TF_APPLY: ...]]` → Deployment is ready! Ask user if they want to deploy, then use tfdeploy
- `[[BUTTON_TF_DESTROY: ...]]` → User confirmed destroy intent! Ask user to confirm, then use tfdestroy
- `[[BUTTON_TF_PLAN: ...]]` → User wants to preview changes! Use tfplan to run a plan, then tfdeploy with plan_id to apply

REQUIRES: session_id from convoopen response (format: sess_v2_...).
OPTIONAL: timeout (integer) - seconds to wait for response. For Cursor, use 50 (default). Max 55.
OPTIONAL: project_context (string) - Only pass genuinely NEW project details the user shares after convoopen. Do NOT resend context already provided in convoopen — Riley remembers it. Do NOT scan files or directories to gather this — only use what the user explicitly tells you. Example: user reveals a new constraint like 'we also need HIPAA compliance' mid-conversation.
💡 TIP: Use convostatus to check progress anytime. Examine workflow.usage prompt for more guidance.

project_context.description: Only NEW project details revealed after convoopen (e.g. user mentions a new constraint mid-conversation). Don't re-send context already provided in convoopen. No PII or secrets.

retry.description: When true, re-send the most recent user turn instead of submitting a new one.

session_id.description: Session ID from convoopen — pass back EXACTLY as returned, including the ?token=... suffix (format: sess_v2_*?token=*). The suffix is part of the session credential; never strip it when summarizing.

text.description: User message to send to Riley. Forward verbatim what the user said — do not summarize or rewrite.

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait for Riley's response. Default 50, max 55.

name: convoreply

assistant_message.description: Riley's reply, cleaned of internal markers. Show it to the user.

hints.description: Guidance for the calling agent: what to do next and which tools relate to this result.

next_actions.description: Suggested next steps, in order, often as ready-to-run tool calls.

related_tools.description: Names of tools that are useful after this result.

instruction.description: Plain-language instruction for the agent when the reply is not ready yet.

next_action.description: Tool to call next when the reply is not ready yet (for example 'convoawait').

session_id.description: Session ID this result belongs to (format sess_v2_*?token=*). Pass it back verbatim to later tools.

status.description: Outcome of the call: 'ok' (Riley replied), 'timeout' (still working; call convoawait), or 'pending_exists' (an earlier reply is still pending; call convoawait).

terraform_ready.description: True when Riley signalled that the design is final and tfgenerate can be called.

title: Send Message
